PORTS: (1) The derivative rework, which is most of the range. f' and f" become MVAR commands in the SOLVE form (fn1stDerivVar/fn2ndDerivVar, TM_SOLVE, PTP_REGISTER): from the keyboard the operand is a program and the MVAR menu opens on it, as a program step the operand is a variable and the program is the one the new PGMDRV named through the new currentDerivProgram global -- a slot of its own so a derivative does not repoint what SOLVE, INT and PLOT run. calcDeriv no longer takes one step and one stencil: it walks h down a decade at a time from x/10, and takes the coarser of the first two same-stencil estimates that agree to within the cancellation the finer one suffers (deriv_agrees), falling back to the coarser member of the closest pair when none ever agrees. Under graphAccActive the tolerance and the ladder length follow SDIGS instead of 34 digits, or the samples would cancel to nothing. A step the user set in the new named variable delta-sub-d is taken as it stands and the ladder is skipped; an infinite value stored there deletes the variable. A sample the function cannot produce becomes a NaN and CLEARS the error (except ERROR_SOLVER_ABORT), which is what stopped the endless goto-failed restart. The old delta-x/delta-X/DELTA-x/DELTA-X label lookup (deriv_default_h, deriv_found_lbl) is gone. In the equation arm the variable's own value is now kept in a register SNAPSHOT across the sampling rather than in TEMP_REGISTER_1, which the user's program could reach; the sole-variable auto-assign is restricted to a formula, since a program's variables are its MVAR declarations. fnSolveVar gained the step key and now RUNS the derivative when an MVAR key is pressed without a preceding entry. New TI_DERIV_STEP (144) and its screen.zig prefix. (2) findProgramLabel in manage.c resolves the operand of every command that KEEPS a program rather than jumping to it -- PGMSLV, PGMINT, PGMPLT, PGMDRV, VARMNU, the sums and products, and the interactive arms of SOLVE, the integral, PLT f and the derivatives -- so all of them accept a local label 00-99 / A-l and all report the same three refusals from one place; note the band FIRST_UC_LOCAL_LABEL (100) .. LAST_LOCAL_LABEL (123) SUBSUMES REGISTER_X..REGISTER_T, and upstream resolves 100-103 as local labels first. fnVarMnu/fn42VarMnu additionally bound the label against numberOfLabels before indexing labelList. (3) The trig caches: WP34S_Atan/Atan2/Asin/Acos and realRectangularToPolar each gained a single most-recent-call slot keyed on the input value(s), the EFFECTIVE compute precision and the rounding mode, with the key and the result written together AFTER the compute so a reentrant call can only leave its own complete pair. realCompareIdentical (a digits/exponent/bits + lsu byte compare, so -0 != +0 and 1 != 1.0) is the key comparison. The polar stack display now computes at a fixed POLAR_DISPLAY_COMPUTE_DIGITS (17+2) instead of a width scaled by the operands' exponent, and convertAngleFromTo runs at that same width; polar_display_cov gates any narrowing. CACHE_DEBUG/CACHE_VERIFY are #undef'd on every target and are not modelled -- but the four result slots ARE 588 bytes of .bss, and the DM42's .bss ends exactly at the DMCP system data block, so `zig build dmcp_pkgs_all` failed the linker ASSERT by 480 bytes. Upstream's own DM42 package-1 build does not link at this pin either (FLASH overflowed by 7512 bytes, measured by building ../c43 at 28fa9ad2e), so there is no upstream answer to follow. A new build option, trig_result_cache, leaves the slots out of the DM42 (OLD_HW) math object and keeps them everywhere else including the parity oracles; a hit returns what a recompute returns, which is exactly what upstream's CACHE_VERIFY build asserts, so the board loses speed and nothing else. The flag is set at the two firmware call sites that build for the board, not inferred from the object name prefix. (4) checkOpCodeOfStep matches the two-byte marker 0x80 instead of masking it off, so the one-byte steps ISE .66 (05 B2) and ISG 18 (06 12) no longer read as END (1458) and REM (1554); the same fix applied to the serialization owner's own isAtEndOfProgram copy. (5) WRITEP and XPORTP restore the whole editor position (step, displayed step, both step numbers, program number) and now restore it on the cancel and write-error paths too; a restored state file recomputes currentLocalStepNumber by counting steps from the restored step POINTER and re-homes an out-of-program pointer; a zero step or program number from an older cfg is repaired to 1; doFnReset seeds both to 1. (6) The status bar and the date/time return without painting while screenHoldsDrawnPixels; showBottomLine draws only when the page asked for a line, and fnC47Show clears the override when it builds the next page and refreshes the screen AFTER it, not before; the menu-clear guards test temporaryInformation != TI_WHO rather than the shared blank menu. (7) execProgram pops any subroutine level left standing by an error, which is what stopped a calling program's own RTN from ever matching. (8) A subroutine return inside a running program no longer forces a status-bar update. (9) Smaller: no key arms a timer while MNU_SHOW is up; a press dismisses the WHO screen only, a real SHOW is handled in processKeyAction; ALL mode clears the digit it rounded so the second rounding pass cannot bump it twice; the DMS fractional seconds are rounded half-up before the uint32 cast; =>DMS in NIM returns when the number did not close; TAM and the key-10 bezel treat F1DRV/F2DRV like SOLVE; isFunctionAllowingNewVariable accepts them. NOT PORTED: nothing. matrixEditor.c's change in range is whitespace only. PORTS: (1) A softkey label too wide for its slot now trades its long right arrow for the short one before any trimming. trimKey measures the compressed label first, returns it whole when it already fits, and otherwise runs the new shortenRightArrows -- an in-place two-byte swap of STD_RIGHT_ARROW for STD_RIGHT_SHORT_ARROW, which is 4 px narrower each -- and returns the label whole if that alone brings it under the limit; only then does the odd/even side trimming run. New MAX_DYNMENU_SLOTS (TMP_STR_LENGTH / 15 = 170) caps the named-variable and reserved-variable loops of _dynmenuConstructVars, the global/local label loop of the PROG/PROGS builder, and both menu-name loops of the MENU/MENUS builder, each of which wrote a fixed 15-byte slot per name with no upper bound on the count. PORTS: (1) THE STATE-FILE CONVERSION the renumbering needs. configFileVersion 10000026 -> 10000028 and BACKUP_VERSION 1017 -> 1019; a file older than the change has its stored menu links moved by the new convertOldMenuNumbers, a 185-entry from/to table applied to the user keyboard and its Norm key, MyMenu, MyAlpha, every user menu (its count clamped to the pool space left after userMenus), and the kbd_usr copy inside every dtConfig register -- global, local and named. doLoad, doLoadDataFile (LOADR and LOADV restore a Conf register) and the backup restore all call it; the backup path also clears lastFunc/lastParam. 10000027 and 1018 default FLAG_M_ALL on. (2) THE MATRIX VIEWER. showRealMatrix's signature changes: the `toDisplay` flag becomes a `dest` buffer -- NULL draws, non-NULL collects a ONE-ROW vector into the caller's own buffer and draws nothing, which is what lets vectorToDisplayString stop borrowing errorMessage (and screen.zig stop saving and restoring it around the call). An empty dest means the viewer refused and the caller shows [n x n Matrix]. The row cap becomes three caps -- 9 under SHOW, 7 under VIEW, 5 on the stack -- and MATRIX_MAX_COLUMNS 11 -> 14. The integer-column rule moves into the new getRealMatrixIntegerColumns so the height cache in createSubstrings and the drawn matrix cannot drift apart, and it gains two tests: ENG/SF/UN are never integer-displayed, and a column past 1E15 leaves integer mode. FLAG_M_ALL (new) gates the ALL-to-SCI/ENG bias in both viewers and in getRealMatrixColumnWidths. An all-integer column is measured at 15 digits and has its trailing radix stripped by the new charString stripTrailingRadix (which display.c's angle34ToDisplayString2 now shares); the column-width sum drops from two inter-column gaps to one plus a 3px end margin, so the fit test measures what the drawing code lays out. A row now steps by the matrix width rather than by the count of columns on screen. The VIEW/SHOW clear becomes one lcd_fill_rect over the matrix area instead of four clearRegisterLine calls. CONSEQUENCE FOR Z47: the relaxed fit means a matrix that just fits MATRIX_LINE_WIDTH (380) leaves no room for the brackets, so X_POS can be negative -- C converts it implicitly to showString's uint32_t, and the owner's checked @intCast panicked on eulersphi.
